---
title: "Examples"
subtitle: "Attributes resolved for HTML."
description: "Each prism prefix applied to a real element, resolved for this HTML page, with the same source resolved for Typst alongside."
---

Every element below carries the attributes shown above it, and the filter resolves them for HTML as this page is rendered.
The [Typst preview](preview.pdf) is the same mechanism resolving the other way.

This site turns on `warn-on-drop`, so a mistyped prefix on these pages is reported rather than lost:

```yaml
extensions:
  prism:
    warn-on-drop: true
```

::: {.callout-important}
## The prefix here is `atelier-html:`, not `html:`

These pages are rendered by the `atelier-html` format, a Quarto custom format built on the HTML writer.
The prefix is matched against the format Quarto is targeting, which is the custom format's own name, so `html:` matches nothing here and `atelier-html:` matches everything.

That is the same rule the [Reference](reference.qmd#which-prefix-matches-which-format) states for `mcanouil-typst` against `typst`, and it is easy to trip over: the attribute simply vanishes.
Turning `warn-on-drop` on was how this page found out.
:::

Because these pages deliberately carry prefixes for formats they are not built as, the render reports a handful of drops every time.
That is the option working, not a fault.

## An exact match

```markdown
::: {atelier-html:style="color: firebrick;" typst:text-fill="rgb(0,0,255)"}
Firebrick here, blue in the PDF.
:::
```

::: {atelier-html:style="color: firebrick;" typst:text-fill="rgb(0,0,255)"}
Firebrick here, blue in the PDF.
:::

The `typst:` attribute is dropped from this page, and the `html:` one from the PDF.

## The default fallback

`default:` applies only when no format-specific variant of the same name matched.

```markdown
::: {default:style="color: grey;" atelier-html:style="color: rebeccapurple;"}
Rebecca purple here, grey everywhere else.
:::
```

::: {default:style="color: grey;" atelier-html:style="color: rebeccapurple;"}
Rebecca purple here, grey everywhere else.
:::

In the [preview](preview.pdf) the same construction resolves to the default, since it names no Typst value.

## The slide alias

`slide:` covers `revealjs`, `slidy`, `s5`, `dzslides`, and `slideous` at once.

```markdown
::: {slide:style="font-size: 2em;"}
Larger on every HTML slide format, ordinary here.
:::
```

::: {slide:style="font-size: 2em;"}
Larger on every HTML slide format, ordinary here.
:::

Nothing applies on this page, because HTML is not a slide format.
An exact prefix beats the alias, so `slide:` and `revealjs:` on one element resolve to the second under `revealjs` and to the first under `slidy`.

## Precedence in one element

```markdown
::: {style="color: grey;" default:style="color: silver;" atelier-html:style="color: crimson;"}
Crimson here.
:::
```

::: {style="color: grey;" default:style="color: silver;" atelier-html:style="color: crimson;"}
Crimson here.
:::

The exact match wins, the default is not needed, and the unprefixed `style` is dropped rather than left to collide, so the element carries one `style` attribute.

## On other elements

It is not only divs.

```markdown
[An inline span]{atelier-html:style="background: gold;"}

## A heading {atelier-html:style="color: teal;"}
```

[An inline span]{atelier-html:style="background: gold;"} sits in this sentence.

### A heading resolved for HTML {atelier-html:style="color: teal;"}

A code block takes them too, which is how a listing is shrunk on a slide without touching the code:

````markdown
```{.r revealjs:style="font-size: 0.6em;"}
1 + 1
```
````

## Catching a typo

An unknown prefix is treated as a format that is not active, and the attribute vanishes.
With `warn-on-drop` on, the render says so instead:

```text
(W) [prism] Dropped attribute(s) 'revaeljs:style' on #mybox because no prefix matched target format 'revealjs'.
```

That is the only way to tell a typo from a deliberately inactive format.
